correctness.rationale: For binary standard Rudin–Shapiro parity r(t)=popcount(t & (t>>1)) mod 2, k>=4, the proof derives the shortest-absent two-choice greedy suffix recurrence; all 12 sixteen-bit block transitions preserve equal option counts with factor 2^(Delta m-4); composition proves |SAS(W)|=2^(iota(W)-4q) for every nonempty word in exactly the four literal blocks. The four-letter morphism and dyadic edge recursion E(2q)=-E(q)-1 yield iota(R_k)=5*2^(k-4)-e_k and |SAS(R_k)|=2^(2^(k-4)-e_k). I independently recomputed all 12 transitions, all 340 block concatenations for q<=4 and full prefixes k=4..12 with a separately written dynamic program; these corroborate the fully described inductive argument.
